issues.detail: draft_markdown contains an embedded question at the end: 'QUESTION: What is the registration number, make, and model of the stolen motorcycle, and on which exact date did the complainant first approach the police station to report the theft?' — the drafter invented a narrative device not found in FACTS and embedded a question as prose in the filing draft.
issues.fix: Remove the 'QUESTION:' paragraph entirely from draft_markdown. Missing facts must appear as [TO CONFIRM] placeholders within the body of the draft, not as a freestanding question appended to the document.

issues.detail: module is 'police' and station_refused is true, but the mandatory SP letter check: the sp_letter_markdown invokes 'Section 173(4) BNSS 2023' in both the subject line and the prayer, yet the sections list for id 'BNSS 173(4)' states the remedy is sending the substance in writing to the SP — the sp_letter_markdown Prayer item 1 says the SP may 'Investigate the matter yourself' which goes beyond what the gist of BNSS 173(4) covers (gist covers only: send substance in writing to SP, who may investigate or direct an officer). However, 'direct a competent police officer to register the FIR and investigate' is supported. The phrase 'Investigate the matter yourself' attributes a power not stated in the provided BNSS 173(4) gist and is an unsupported claim.
issues.fix: In sp_letter_markdown Prayer item 1, remove the sub-bullet 'Investigate the matter yourself; or' and retain only 'Direct a competent police officer to register the FIR and investigate the cognizable offence of theft,' to stay within the scope of the BNSS 173(4) gist provided.

issues.detail: sections entry id 'BNSS 173' — why states the officer was 'legally bound to register an FIR upon receiving information of this cognizable offence'; the gist of BNSS 173 notes that a preliminary enquiry is allowed in limited cases (3–7 yr punishment) before registration. The why does not acknowledge this qualification and overstates the scope by asserting an absolute duty without caveat, inconsistent with the gist.
issues.fix: Amend the 'why' for BNSS 173 to note that for cognizable offences outside the preliminary-enquiry exception (3–7 yr punishment range), registration is mandatory; or add a [TO CONFIRM] noting that the applicable punishment range should be confirmed by the supervising advocate to ensure the preliminary-enquiry exception does not apply.
